title: Goal Parser Interpretation
statement: The string `command` is a sequence of three kinds of tokens written back to back: `"G"`, `"()"` and `"(al)"`. Translate it token by token, turning `"G"` into `"G"`, `"()"` into `"o"` and `"(al)"` into `"al"`, and return the translations joined in their original order.
constraints: command is made only of the tokens "G", "()" and "(al)", in any order
notes:
## Intuition

Each token is recognisable from its first one or two characters: a `'G'` is the whole token, and after a `'('` the next character tells `"()"` (a `')'`) apart from `"(al)"` (an `'a'`). So a single left-to-right scan can read one token at a time, append its translation, and jump past it. The simpler alternative replaces every `"(al)"` with `"al"` and every `"()"` with `"o"` using string replacement.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `result` and `i = 0`.
2. While `i` is inside `command`:
   - If `command[i]` is `'G'`, append `"G"` and move `i` by 1.
   - Otherwise it is a `'('`. If `command[i + 1]` is `')'`, the token is `"()"`: append `"o"` and move by 2.
   - Otherwise the token is `"(al)"`: append `"al"` and move by 4.
3. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

For `command = "G()(al)"`: at `i = 0` the character is `'G'`, so `result = "G"` and `i = 1`. At `i = 1` the next character is `')'`, so `result = "Go"` and `i = 3`. At `i = 3` the next character is `'a'`, so `result = "Goal"` and `i = 7`, the end of the string. The answer is `"Goal"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is looked at a constant number of times.
- Space: O(n) for the output string.

## Pitfalls

- Advance by the token's full length (1, 2 or 4); moving one character at a time would read `"al"` and `")"` as new tokens.
- Peek at `command[i + 1]`, not `command[i]`, to tell `"()"` from `"(al)"`: both start with `'('`.
- If you use replacement instead, replace every occurrence, not just the first.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | the translation built so far |
| `i` | index of the first character of the next unread token |

narration.3: i always points at the start of the next token.
narration.5: Read tokens until the whole command is used up.
narration.6: A 'G' is a complete token by itself.
narration.9: Otherwise the token starts with '('; a ')' right after it means the token is "()".
narration.13: The only remaining token is "(al)", which translates to "al".
